bibl.title: A large-scale standardized physiological survey reveals functional organization of the mouse visual cortex

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how stimulus representations ARE TRANSFORMED THROUGHOUT THE VISUAL CORTEX, surveyed rather than sampled
span.quote: To understand how the brain processes sensory information to guide behavior, we must know how stimulus representations are transformed throughout the visual cortex. Here we report an open, large-scale physiological survey of activity in the awake mouse visual cortex: the Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding dataset. This publicly available dataset includes cortical activity from nearly 60,000 neurons from 6 visual areas, 4 layers, and 12 transgenic mouse lines from 243 adult mice, in response to a systematic set of visual stimuli. We classify neurons based on joint reliabilities to multiple stimuli and validate this functional classification with models of visual responses. While most classes are characterized by responses to specific subsets of the stimuli, the largest class is not reliably responsive to any of the stimuli and becomes progressively larger in higher visual areas. These classes reveal a functional organization wherein putative dorsal areas show specialization for visual motion signals.

span.label: whether the standard account of visual cortex survives a survey that does not select its neurons by their responses - A KEY CHALLENGE RESULTS FROM THE FACT THAT THIS UNDERSTANDING IS BASED ON MANY SMALL STUDIES, RECORDING RESPONSES FROM DIFFERENT STAGES IN THE CIRCUIT, USING DIFFERENT STIMULI AND ANALYSES
span.quote: A key challenge results from the fact that this understanding is based on many small studies, recording responses from different stages in the circuit, using different stimuli and analyses 5 . The inherent experimental selection biases and lack of standardization of this approach introduce additional obstacles to creating a cohesive understanding of cortical function.

span.label: an open survey in which THE LARGEST CLASS IS NOT RELIABLY RESPONSIVE TO ANY OF THE STIMULI AND BECOMES PROGRESSIVELY LARGER IN HIGHER VISUAL AREAS

span.label: existence
span.quote: While most classes are characterized by responses to specific subsets of the stimuli, the largest class is not reliably responsive to any of the stimuli and becomes progressively larger in higher visual areas.

span.label: functional organization of mouse visual cortex
span.quote: These classes reveal a functional organization wherein putative dorsal areas show specialization for visual motion signals.

span.label: two-photon-calcium-imaging
span.quote: Calcium imaging was performed using a two-photon-imaging instrument (either a Scientifica Vivoscope or a Nikon A1R MP+; the Nikon system was adapted to provide space to accommodate the running disk).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Hand-tuning stimuli to each recorded neuron builds selection bias into the classical literature, which is why the standard model looks better in small studies than in an unbiased survey.
span.quote: The inherent experimental selection biases and lack of standardization of this approach introduce additional obstacles to creating a cohesive understanding of cortical function.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The unresponsive 'none' neurons may in fact be visually driven but tuned to highly sparse, specific natural features constructed by hierarchical processing, which the presented stimulus set never hits.
span.quote: It is possible these neurons are visually driven, but are responsive to highly sparse and specific natural features that may arise through hierarchical processing 37 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because responses are so sparse, different neurons are active at different moments, which is what keeps their pairwise noise correlations weak.
span.quote: Such high sparseness suggests that neurons are active at different times and thus their activities are weakly correlated.

span.label: the bias this survey is built against, described as a procedure: NEURONS WERE IDENTIFIED BY RESPONDING TO A TEST STIMULUS - THE STIMULUS WAS THEN HAND-TUNED TO ELICIT THE STRONGEST RELIABLE RESPONSE FROM THAT NEURON, AND THE EXPERIMENT PROCEEDED USING MANIPULATIONS AROUND THIS CONDITION
span.quote: Historically, visual physiology has been dominated by single-neuron electrophysiological recordings in which neurons were identified by responding to a test stimulus. The stimulus was then hand-tuned to elicit the strongest reliable response from that neuron, and the experiment proceeded using manipulations around this condition. Such studies discovered many characteristic response properties, namely that visual responses can be characterized by combinations of linear filters with nonlinearities such as half-wave rectification, squaring, and response normalization 7 , or that neurons (in V1 at least) largely cluster into “simple” and “complex” cells. But these studies may have failed to capture the variability of responses, the breadth of features that will elicit a neural response, and the breadth of features that do not elicit a response. This results in systematic bias in the measurement of neurons and a confirmation bias regarding model assumptions.

span.label: and what that procedure cannot see: THESE STUDIES MAY HAVE FAILED TO CAPTURE THE VARIABILITY OF RESPONSES, THE BREADTH OF FEATURES THAT WILL ELICIT A NEURAL RESPONSE, AND THE BREADTH OF FEATURES THAT DO NOT ELICIT A RESPONSE - THIS RESULTS IN SYSTEMATIC BIAS IN THE MEASUREMENT OF NEURONS AND A CONFIRMATION BIAS REGARDING MODEL ASSUMPTIONS
span.quote: Historically, visual physiology has been dominated by single-neuron electrophysiological recordings in which neurons were identified by responding to a test stimulus. The stimulus was then hand-tuned to elicit the strongest reliable response from that neuron, and the experiment proceeded using manipulations around this condition. Such studies discovered many characteristic response properties, namely that visual responses can be characterized by combinations of linear filters with nonlinearities such as half-wave rectification, squaring, and response normalization 7 , or that neurons (in V1 at least) largely cluster into “simple” and “complex” cells. But these studies may have failed to capture the variability of responses, the breadth of features that will elicit a neural response, and the breadth of features that do not elicit a response. This results in systematic bias in the measurement of neurons and a confirmation bias regarding model assumptions.

span.label: the one design decision that removes it: THIS PIPELINE REDUCED CRITICAL EXPERIMENTAL BIASES BY SEPARATING QUALITY CONTROL OF DATA COLLECTION FROM RESPONSE CHARACTERIZATION
span.quote: This pipeline reduced critical experimental biases by separating quality control of data collection from response characterization. Such a survey is crucial for assessing the successes and shortcomings of contemporary models of visual cortex.

span.label: and the reason it matters for a whole literature: THIS UNDERSTANDING IS BASED ON MANY SMALL STUDIES, RECORDING RESPONSES FROM DIFFERENT STAGES IN THE CIRCUIT, USING DIFFERENT STIMULI AND ANALYSES - THE INHERENT EXPERIMENTAL SELECTION BIASES AND LACK OF STANDARDIZATION OF THIS APPROACH INTRODUCE ADDITIONAL OBSTACLES TO CREATING A COHESIVE UNDERSTANDING OF CORTICAL FUNCTION
span.quote: A key challenge results from the fact that this understanding is based on many small studies, recording responses from different stages in the circuit, using different stimuli and analyses 5 . The inherent experimental selection biases and lack of standardization of this approach introduce additional obstacles to creating a cohesive understanding of cortical function.

span.label: The putative ventral higher visual areas could not be imaged, so the expected inverse (spatial-over-motion) organisation could not be tested.
span.quote: The lack of an inverse relationship, wherein spatial information is overrepresented relative to motion in a putative “ventral” stream, likely reflects the fact that we were unable to image the putative ventral areas LI, POR, or P within our cranial window.

span.label: Neurons classed as responding only to natural stimuli may be conventional cells tuned to spatial or temporal frequencies the stimulus set did not sample.
span.quote: It is possible these neurons could be “classical” neurons as well but are tuned for spatial or temporal frequencies that were not included in our stimulus set.

span.label: The wavelet models leave a large amount of visually responsive activity unexplained.
span.quote: It is also worth noting that there is a great deal of visually responsive activity that is not being captured by these models ( Supplementary Figure 5 ).

span.label: The epileptiform-event screening used to exclude mice could not be applied to the inhibitory Cre lines.
span.quote: Inhibitory lines were excluded from this analysis as the neuronal labelling was too sparse to reliably assess these events from normal spontaneous activity.

span.label: one half of the expected organisation is missing for a reason that is about the window, not the brain - WE WERE UNABLE TO IMAGE THE PUTATIVE VENTRAL AREAS LI, POR, OR P WITHIN OUR CRANIAL WINDOW
span.quote: The lack of an inverse relationship, wherein spatial information is overrepresented relative to motion in a putative “ventral” stream, likely reflects the fact that we were unable to image the putative ventral areas LI, POR, or P within our cranial window.

span.label: the largest class may be an artefact of the stimulus set rather than a property of the cells - IT IS POSSIBLE THESE NEURONS ARE VISUALLY DRIVEN, BUT ARE RESPONSIVE TO HIGHLY SPARSE AND SPECIFIC NATURAL FEATURES, or THESE NEURONS COULD BE INVOLVED IN NON-VISUAL COMPUTATION
span.quote: What, then, do these neurons do? It is possible these neurons are visually driven, but are responsive to highly sparse and specific natural features that may arise through hierarchical processing 37 . Indeed, the field has a growing body of evidence that the rodent visual system exhibits sophisticated computations. For instance, neurons as early as V1 show visual responses to complex stimulus patterns 38 . Alternatively, these neurons could be involved in non-visual computation, including behavioral responses such as reward timing and sequence learning 39 , as well as modulation by multimodal sensory stimuli 39 , 40 and motor signals 24 , 26 , 41 – 43 . While we found little evidence that these neurons were correlated with the mouse’s running recent work has found running to be among the least predictive such motor signals

span.label: and the stimulus parameters may have been set too low - AS OUR STIMULUS PARAMETERS WERE CHOSEN TO MATCH PREVIOUS MEASUREMENTS OF MOUSE ACUITY, THIS COULD SUGGEST THAT THE ACUITY OF MOUSE HAS BEEN UNDERESTIMATED
span.quote: Neurons in the “NS-NM” class show equally high prediction for natural stimuli, but poor prediction for artificial stimuli ( Figure 7f ). It is possible these neurons could be “classical” neurons as well but are tuned for spatial or temporal frequencies that were not included in our stimulus set. As our stimulus parameters were chosen to match previous measurements of mouse acuity, this could suggest that the acuity of mouse has been underestimated

span.label: the models fail for most of the cortex - EVEN WITH THE INCLUSION OF RUNNING, OUR MODELS PREDICT RESPONSES IN A MINORITY OF NEURONS
span.quote: The true test of a model is its ability to predict arbitrary novel responses, in addition to responses from stimuli used for characterization. Even with the inclusion of running, our models predict responses in a minority of neurons ( Figure 7 ). Neurons in the “DG-SG-NS-NM” class were well predicted, with values comparable to those found in primates 7 , 11 , 34 , 35 , for both natural and artificial stimuli ( Figure 7g ). Based on the way we chose our stimulus parameters, we expect that neurons with a strong “classical receptive field” would be most likely to appear in this class. However, this class constitutes only 10% of the mouse visual cortex

span.label: the pipeline itself - STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES WITH INTEGRATED ENGINEERING TOOLS, applied to make 243 mice comparable to each other
span.quote: Here we scaled calcium imaging, combining standard operating procedures with integrated engineering tools to address some of the challenges of this difficult technique, to create an unprecedented survey of 59,610 neurons in mouse visual cortex, across 243 mice, using a standard and well-studied but diverse set of visual stimuli.

span.label: quality control of the recording separated from characterisation of the response
span.quote: This survey was executed in pipeline fashion, with standardized equipment and protocols and with strict quality control measures not dependent upon stimulus-driven activity

span.label: the functional classes validated against a model containing the standard machinery plus running speed
span.quote: The true test of a model is its ability to predict arbitrary novel responses, in addition to responses from stimuli used for characterization. Even with the inclusion of running, our models predict responses in a minority of neurons ( Figure 7 ). Neurons in the “DG-SG-NS-NM” class were well predicted, with values comparable to those found in primates 7 , 11 , 34 , 35 , for both natural and artificial stimuli ( Figure 7g ). Based on the way we chose our stimulus parameters, we expect that neurons with a strong “classical receptive field” would be most likely to appear in this class. However, this class constitutes only 10% of the mouse visual cortex

span.label: both artificial and natural stimuli presented to the same neurons
span.quote: Further, it is known that stimulus statistics affect visual responses, such that responses to natural scenes cannot be well predicted by responses to noise or grating stimuli 10 – 15 . To examine the extent of this discrepancy and its variation across areas and layers, we designed a stimulus set that included both artificial (gratings and noise) and natural (scenes and movies) stimuli. While artificial stimuli can be easily parameterized and interpreted, natural stimuli are closer to what is ethologically relevant.

span.label: running checked as an explanation for the unresponsive class
span.quote: What, then, do these neurons do? It is possible these neurons are visually driven, but are responsive to highly sparse and specific natural features that may arise through hierarchical processing 37 . Indeed, the field has a growing body of evidence that the rodent visual system exhibits sophisticated computations. For instance, neurons as early as V1 show visual responses to complex stimulus patterns 38 . Alternatively, these neurons could be involved in non-visual computation, including behavioral responses such as reward timing and sequence learning 39 , as well as modulation by multimodal sensory stimuli 39 , 40 and motor signals 24 , 26 , 41 – 43 . While we found little evidence that these neurons were correlated with the mouse’s running recent work has found running to be among the least predictive such motor signals

span.label: a STANDARDISED survey - fixed operating procedures and stimuli applied identically across 59,610 neurons in 243 mice - in place of experiment-specific stimulus choices
span.quote: This results in systematic bias in the measurement of neurons and a confirmation bias regarding model assumptions.

span.label: THE LARGEST CLASS OF NEURONS RESPONDS TO NOTHING: REMARKABLY, THE LARGEST CLASS OF NEURONS WAS THE “none” CLASS, CONSTITUTING THOSE NEURONS THAT DID NOT RESPOND RELIABLY TO ANY OF THE STIMULI (34% OF NEURONS) - THESE NEURONS ARE THE LEAST LIKELY TO BE DESCRIBED BY “CLASSICAL RECEPTIVE FIELDS,” AS EVIDENCED BY THEIR POOR MODEL PERFORMANCE FOR ALL STIMULI
span.quote: Remarkably, the largest class of neurons was the “none” class, constituting those neurons that did not respond reliably to any of the stimuli (34% of neurons). These neurons are the least likely to be described by “classical receptive fields,” as evidenced by their poor model performance for all stimuli

span.label: and in one area it is almost everything: AREA RL HAS THE LARGEST PROPORTION OF NEURONS IN THE “none” CLASS, OVER 85%, CONSISTENT WITH THE VERY LOW PERCENT OF RESPONSIVE NEURONS
span.quote: Area RL has the largest proportion of neurons in the “none” class, over 85%, consistent with the very low percent of responsive neurons ( Figure 2 ). It is possible that neurons in this area are specialized for visual features not probed here, or that they show a greater degree of multi-modality than in the other visual areas, integrating somatosensory and visual features

span.label: THE PAPER ASKS THE QUESTION ITSELF AND LEAVES IT OPEN: WHAT, THEN, DO THESE NEURONS DO? - and offers both readings, that they ARE RESPONSIVE TO HIGHLY SPARSE AND SPECIFIC NATURAL FEATURES or COULD BE INVOLVED IN NON-VISUAL COMPUTATION
span.quote: What, then, do these neurons do? It is possible these neurons are visually driven, but are responsive to highly sparse and specific natural features that may arise through hierarchical processing 37 . Indeed, the field has a growing body of evidence that the rodent visual system exhibits sophisticated computations. For instance, neurons as early as V1 show visual responses to complex stimulus patterns 38 . Alternatively, these neurons could be involved in non-visual computation, including behavioral responses such as reward timing and sequence learning 39 , as well as modulation by multimodal sensory stimuli 39 , 40 and motor signals 24 , 26 , 41 – 43 . While we found little evidence that these neurons were correlated with the mouse’s running recent work has found running to be among the least predictive such motor signals

span.label: THE CLASS THE STANDARD MODEL EXPLAINS IS A TENTH OF THE CORTEX: NEURONS IN THE “DG-SG-NS-NM” CLASS WERE WELL PREDICTED, WITH VALUES COMPARABLE TO THOSE FOUND IN PRIMATES - HOWEVER, THIS CLASS CONSTITUTES ONLY 10% OF THE MOUSE VISUAL CORTEX. And EVEN WITH THE INCLUSION OF RUNNING, OUR MODELS PREDICT RESPONSES IN A MINORITY OF NEURONS
span.quote: The true test of a model is its ability to predict arbitrary novel responses, in addition to responses from stimuli used for characterization. Even with the inclusion of running, our models predict responses in a minority of neurons ( Figure 7 ). Neurons in the “DG-SG-NS-NM” class were well predicted, with values comparable to those found in primates 7 , 11 , 34 , 35 , for both natural and artificial stimuli ( Figure 7g ). Based on the way we chose our stimulus parameters, we expect that neurons with a strong “classical receptive field” would be most likely to appear in this class. However, this class constitutes only 10% of the mouse visual cortex

span.label: THE SELECTION BIAS OF A WHOLE LITERATURE, DESCRIBED AS A PROCEDURE: NEURONS WERE IDENTIFIED BY RESPONDING TO A TEST STIMULUS - THE STIMULUS WAS THEN HAND-TUNED TO ELICIT THE STRONGEST RELIABLE RESPONSE FROM THAT NEURON... THIS RESULTS IN SYSTEMATIC BIAS IN THE MEASUREMENT OF NEURONS AND A CONFIRMATION BIAS REGARDING MODEL ASSUMPTIONS
span.quote: Historically, visual physiology has been dominated by single-neuron electrophysiological recordings in which neurons were identified by responding to a test stimulus. The stimulus was then hand-tuned to elicit the strongest reliable response from that neuron, and the experiment proceeded using manipulations around this condition. Such studies discovered many characteristic response properties, namely that visual responses can be characterized by combinations of linear filters with nonlinearities such as half-wave rectification, squaring, and response normalization 7 , or that neurons (in V1 at least) largely cluster into “simple” and “complex” cells. But these studies may have failed to capture the variability of responses, the breadth of features that will elicit a neural response, and the breadth of features that do not elicit a response. This results in systematic bias in the measurement of neurons and a confirmation bias regarding model assumptions.

span.label: and the fix is one sentence of study design: THIS PIPELINE REDUCED CRITICAL EXPERIMENTAL BIASES BY SEPARATING QUALITY CONTROL OF DATA COLLECTION FROM RESPONSE CHARACTERIZATION - the decision to include a cell is made before anyone knows whether it responds
span.quote: This pipeline reduced critical experimental biases by separating quality control of data collection from response characterization. Such a survey is crucial for assessing the successes and shortcomings of contemporary models of visual cortex.

span.label: THE PROBLEM STATED AS A PROBLEM OF SYNTHESIS: THIS UNDERSTANDING IS BASED ON MANY SMALL STUDIES, RECORDING RESPONSES FROM DIFFERENT STAGES IN THE CIRCUIT, USING DIFFERENT STIMULI AND ANALYSES - THE INHERENT EXPERIMENTAL SELECTION BIASES AND LACK OF STANDARDIZATION OF THIS APPROACH INTRODUCE ADDITIONAL OBSTACLES TO CREATING A COHESIVE UNDERSTANDING OF CORTICAL FUNCTION
span.quote: A key challenge results from the fact that this understanding is based on many small studies, recording responses from different stages in the circuit, using different stimuli and analyses 5 . The inherent experimental selection biases and lack of standardization of this approach introduce additional obstacles to creating a cohesive understanding of cortical function.

span.label: and the field asked for exactly this: INFLUENTIAL REVIEWS HAVE QUESTIONED THE VALIDITY OF THIS STANDARD MODEL, AND HAVE ARGUED THAT “WHAT WOULD BE MOST HELPFUL IS TO ACCUMULATE A DATABASE OF SINGLE UNIT OR MULTI-UNIT DATA THAT WOULD ALLOW MODELERS TO TEST THEIR BEST THEORY UNDER ECOLOGICAL CONDITIONS.”
span.quote: On the basis of these issues, influential reviews have questioned the validity of this standard model 5 – 7 , and have argued that “What would be most helpful is to accumulate a database of single unit or multi-unit data that would allow modelers to test their best theory under ecological conditions.

span.label: A MISSING HALF OF THE ANSWER, ATTRIBUTED TO THE WINDOW AND NOT THE BRAIN: THE LACK OF AN INVERSE RELATIONSHIP, WHEREIN SPATIAL INFORMATION IS OVERREPRESENTED RELATIVE TO MOTION IN A PUTATIVE “VENTRAL” STREAM, LIKELY REFLECTS THE FACT THAT WE WERE UNABLE TO IMAGE THE PUTATIVE VENTRAL AREAS LI, POR, OR P WITHIN OUR CRANIAL WINDOW
span.quote: The lack of an inverse relationship, wherein spatial information is overrepresented relative to motion in a putative “ventral” stream, likely reflects the fact that we were unable to image the putative ventral areas LI, POR, or P within our cranial window.

span.label: TWO INTERNEURON CLASSES, 94% AGAINST 9%, TO THE SAME STIMULUS: 94% OF Sst NEURONS IN V1 ARE RESPONSIVE TO DRIFTING GRATINGS, AND RESPOND QUITE RELIABLY ACROSS TRIALS, FAR MORE THAN THE OTHER CRE LINES - Vip NEURONS, ON THE OTHER HAND, ARE LARGELY UNRESPONSIVE, EVEN SUPPRESSED, BY DRIFTING GRATINGS, WITH ONLY 9% OF Vip NEURONS IN V1 LABELLED RESPONSIVE
span.quote: Sst neurons are strongly driven by all visual stimuli used here, with the plurality belonging to the “DG-SG-NS-NM” class ( Figure 5f ). Their responses to drifting gratings are particularly robust in that 94% of Sst neurons in V1 are responsive to drifting gratings, and respond quite reliably across trials, far more than the other Cre lines ( Extended Data 3 , Supplementary Figure 5 ). Vip neurons, on the other hand, are largely unresponsive, even suppressed, by drifting gratings, with only 9% of Vip neurons in V1 labelled responsive.

span.label: and the same cells are highly responsive to a different stimulus class: Vip NEURONS ARE VERY RESPONSIVE TO BOTH NATURAL SCENES AND NATURAL MOVIES, but SHOW LITTLE SELECTIVITY TO THESE STIMULI, AS THEIR MEDIAN LIFETIME SPARSENESS IS LOWER THAN BOTH THE Sst AND THE EXCITATORY NEURONS. `Vip cells are unresponsive` is true of one stimulus set and false of another
span.quote: Vip neurons, however, are very responsive to both natural scenes and natural movies, the majority falling in the “NS-NM” class ( Figure 6f , Extended Data 6 , 7 , Supplementary Figure 8 ), but show little selectivity to these stimuli, as their median lifetime sparseness is lower than both the Sst and the excitatory neurons

span.label: A MEASUREMENT THAT REVERSES AN EARLIER ONE, WITH THE STIMULUS NAMED: RECEPTIVE FIELD MAPPING USING LOCALLY SPARSE NOISE REVEALED THAT Vip NEURONS IN V1 HAVE REMARKABLY LARGE RECEPTIVE FIELD AREAS, LARGER THAN BOTH Sst AND EXCITATORY NEURONS, IN CONTRAST TO THE SMALLER SUMMATION AREA FOR Vip NEURONS, PREVIOUSLY MEASURED USING WINDOWED DRIFTING GRATINGS
span.quote: Interestingly, receptive field mapping using locally sparse noise revealed that Vip neurons in V1 have remarkably large receptive field areas, larger than both Sst and excitatory neurons ( Figure 3f ), in contrast to the smaller summation area for Vip neurons, previously measured using windowed drifting gratings 23 , 33 . This suggests that Vip neurons respond to small features over a large region of space.

span.label: THE STIMULUS CLASS DECIDES THE ANSWER, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO BEFORE MEASURING: IT IS KNOWN THAT STIMULUS STATISTICS AFFECT VISUAL RESPONSES, SUCH THAT RESPONSES TO NATURAL SCENES CANNOT BE WELL PREDICTED BY RESPONSES TO NOISE OR GRATING STIMULI - WHILE ARTIFICIAL STIMULI CAN BE EASILY PARAMETERIZED AND INTERPRETED, NATURAL STIMULI ARE CLOSER TO WHAT IS ETHOLOGICALLY RELEVANT
span.quote: Further, it is known that stimulus statistics affect visual responses, such that responses to natural scenes cannot be well predicted by responses to noise or grating stimuli 10 – 15 . To examine the extent of this discrepancy and its variation across areas and layers, we designed a stimulus set that included both artificial (gratings and noise) and natural (scenes and movies) stimuli. While artificial stimuli can be easily parameterized and interpreted, natural stimuli are closer to what is ethologically relevant.

span.label: the headline positive, with its complement: 77% OF NEURONS IN THE MOUSE VISUAL CORTEX RESPOND TO AT LEAST ONE OF THESE VISUAL STIMULI - and THE RESPONSES TO ALL STIMULI ARE HIGHLY SPARSE AND VARIABLE
span.quote: We find that 77% of neurons in the mouse visual cortex respond to at least one of these visual stimuli, many showing classical tuning properties, such as orientation and direction selective responses to gratings. These tuning properties exhibit differences across cortical areas and Cre lines. While subtle differences do exist between the excitatory Cre lines, these populations are largely similar; the more marked differences are among the inhibitory interneurons. The responses to all stimuli are highly sparse and variable.

span.label: THE DIFFERENCES ARE BETWEEN THE INHIBITORY LINES, NOT THE EXCITATORY ONES: WHILE SUBTLE DIFFERENCES DO EXIST BETWEEN THE EXCITATORY CRE LINES, THESE POPULATIONS ARE LARGELY SIMILAR; THE MORE MARKED DIFFERENCES ARE AMONG THE INHIBITORY INTERNEURONS
span.quote: We find that 77% of neurons in the mouse visual cortex respond to at least one of these visual stimuli, many showing classical tuning properties, such as orientation and direction selective responses to gratings. These tuning properties exhibit differences across cortical areas and Cre lines. While subtle differences do exist between the excitatory Cre lines, these populations are largely similar; the more marked differences are among the inhibitory interneurons. The responses to all stimuli are highly sparse and variable.

span.label: and yet the excitatory lines are not interchangeable either: RORB, SCNN1A-TG3, AND NR5A1, WHICH LABEL DISTINCT LAYER 4 POPULATIONS IN V1, EXHIBIT DISTINCT SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL TUNING PROPERTIES, DIFFERENT DEGREES OF RUNNING CORRELATION, AND SUBTLE DIFFERENCES IN THEIR CLASS DISTRIBUTION - THESE DIFFERENCES SUGGEST THAT THERE ARE SEPARATE CHANNELS OF FEEDFORWARD INFORMATION
span.quote: On a coarse scale, excitatory populations behave similarly; however, closer examination reveals distinct functional properties across Cre lines. For instance, Rorb, Scnn1a-Tg3, and Nr5a1, which label distinct layer 4 populations in V1, exhibit distinct spatial and temporal tuning properties ( Figure 3 , Supplementary Figure 1 , 2 ), different degrees of running correlation ( Figure 5 ), and subtle differences in their class distribution ( Figure 6 ). These differences suggest that there are separate channels of feedforward information. Similar differences between Fezf2 and Ntsr1 in V1, which label two distinct populations of corticofugal neurons found in layers 5 and 6 respectively, indicate distinct feedback channels from V1.

span.label: THE CLASSES DO NOT RESPECT THE AREAS: THE DIFFERENT CLASSES ARE LARGELY INTERMINGLED, AND FOUND IN ALL OF THE CORTICAL AREAS RECORDED HERE, SUGGESTING A LARGELY PARALLEL ORGANIZATION
span.quote: The different classes are largely intermingled, and found in all of the cortical areas recorded here, suggesting a largely parallel organization

span.label: and what organisation there is comes from proportions rather than presence: THE OVERREPRESENTATION OF CLASSES RESPONSIVE TO NATURAL MOVIES AND MOTION STIMULI IN AREAS AL, PM, AND AM RELATIVE TO THE OTHER CLASSES IS CONSISTENT WITH THE ASSIGNMENT OF THESE AREAS TO THE PUTATIVE “DORSAL” OR “MOTION” STREAM
span.quote: At the same time, the overrepresentation of classes responsive to natural movies and motion stimuli in areas AL, PM, and AM relative to the other classes (which are more responsive to spatial stimuli) is consistent with the assignment of these areas to the putative “dorsal” or “motion” stream

span.label: THE DATASET IS THE CONTRIBUTION AND IT IS ALREADY BEING REUSED: THESE DATA HAVE BEEN USED BY OTHER RESEARCHERS TO DEVELOP IMAGE PROCESSING METHODS, TO EXAMINE STIMULUS ENCODING AND DECODING, AND TO TEST MODELS OF CORTICAL COMPUTATIONS
span.quote: We believe that the openly available Allen Brain Observatory provides an important foundational resource for the community. In addition to providing an experimental benchmark, these data serve as a testbed for theories and models. Already, these data have been used by other researchers to develop image processing methods 44 , 45 , to examine stimulus encoding and decoding 46 – 49 , and to test models of cortical computations

span.label: builds-on → Jewell et al. L0-penalized event detection method
span.quote: We used the L0-penalized method of Jewell, et al for event detection 17 , 71 .

span.label: builds-on → Vinje and Gallant definition of lifetime sparseness
span.quote: Lifetime sparseness was computed using the definition in Vinje and Gallant 20 .

span.label: builds-on → Schoppe et al. computation of CCmax
span.quote: We follow the computation from Schoppe, et al . 76 :

This results in systematic bias in the measurement of neurons and a confirmation bias regarding model assumptions.

This suggests that Vip neurons respond to small features over a large region of space.

span.quote: Further, it is known that stimulus statistics affect visual responses, such that responses to natural scenes cannot be well predicted by responses to noise or grating stimuli 10 – 15 . To examine the extent of this discrepancy and its variation across areas and layers, we designed a stimulus set that included both artificial (gratings and noise) and natural (scenes and movies) stimuli. span.label: bias —causes→ model
span.note: THIS RESULTS IN SYSTEMATIC BIAS IN THE MEASUREMENT OF NEURONS AND A CONFIRMATION BIAS REGARDING MODEL ASSUMPTIONS
span.quote: Historically, visual physiology has been dominated by single-neuron electrophysiological recordings in which neurons were identified by responding to a test stimulus. The stimulus was then hand-tuned to elicit the strongest reliable response from that neuron, and the experiment proceeded using manipulations around this condition. Such studies discovered many characteristic response properties, namely that visual responses can be characterized by combinations of linear filters with nonlinearities such as half-wave rectification, squaring, and response normalization 7 , or that neurons (in V1 at least) largely cluster into “simple” and “complex” cells. But these studies may have failed to capture the variability of responses, the breadth of features that will elicit a neural response, and the breadth of features that do not elicit a response. This results in systematic bias in the measurement of neurons and a confirmation bias regarding model assumptions.

The responses to all stimuli are highly sparse and variable.

span.label: 94% — of Sst neurons in V1 responsive to drifting gratings
span.quote: Sst neurons are strongly driven by all visual stimuli used here, with the plurality belonging to the “DG-SG-NS-NM” class ( Figure 5f ). Their responses to drifting gratings are particularly robust in that 94% of Sst neurons in V1 are responsive to drifting gratings, and respond quite reliably across trials, far more than the other Cre lines ( Extended Data 3 , Supplementary Figure 5 ). Vip neurons, on the other hand, are largely unresponsive, even suppressed, by drifting gratings, with only 9% of Vip neurons in V1 labelled responsive.

span.label: over 85% — of neurons in area RL falling in the `none` class
span.quote: Area RL has the largest proportion of neurons in the “none” class, over 85%, consistent with the very low percent of responsive neurons ( Figure 2 ). It is possible that neurons in this area are specialized for visual features not probed here, or that they show a greater degree of multi-modality than in the other visual areas, integrating somatosensory and visual features
